title: Akbar Socio Religious The Second Phase 1573 80 The Ibadat Khana
definition: The second phase of Akbar's religious policy (1573-1580) marks the transition from orthodox Islamic adherence to a policy of 'Sulh-i-kul' (universal peace), institutionalized by the establishment of the Ibadat Khana (House of Worship) at Fatehpur Sikri in 1575.
importanceInUpsc: This topic is central to understanding the evolution of Mughal secularism, the role of the Ulema in state affairs, and the intellectual synthesis of Akbar's reign, frequently appearing in Prelims (chronology/concepts) and Mains (state-religion relations).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Akbar Socio Religious The Second Phase 1573 80 The Ibadat Khana.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Role of the Ulema in the 16th century
